telemetry_stall.description: Freeze the vehicle-side publisher so createdDateTime stops advancing while the rFMS API stays up.
expected_symptoms: createdDateTime stops advancing; data age grows past stale_threshold_s
risks: Zenoh session lease may expire during a long pause and require reconnect on unpause
Telemetry for the paused window is not produced (no backfill)

service_crash.description: Crash the vehicle-side publisher (docker stop: SIGTERM, SIGKILL after stop_timeout_s) and restart it.
expected_symptoms: HYPOTHESIS: createdDateTime stops advancing; data age grows past stale_threshold_s
HYPOTHESIS: after docker start, fresh data takes longer to return than after unpause (cold databroker + Zenoh reconnect)
risks: fms-forwarder has no restart policy: if docker start fails it stays down (rollback not verified -> LATCHED_UNSAFE)
Zenoh client may reconnect slowly or not at all after a cold start
Telemetry for the stopped window is never produced (no backfill)

dependency_failure.description: Stop the shared time-series store (docker stop) and start it again. Expected symptom: the rFMS API answers with an error status instead of data.
expected_symptoms: HYPOTHESIS: fms-server answers HTTP 500 (source: fms-server/src/lib.rs maps query errors to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR), i.e. the failure is VISIBLE to a plain health check
HYPOTHESIS: fms-consumer keeps running but drops the statuses it cannot write (influx-client writer.rs: 'failed to write data to influx'), leaving a gap in stored data after recovery
HYPOTHESIS: no container other than influxDB changes state (fms-server, fms-consumer, grafana keep running)
MEASURED Day 2 (strict 2 s rule): fms-server does not answer within 2 s while influxDB is down (~2 s connect failure, or blocks until influxDB returns); envelope 5 s added to observe the full profile
risks: Wider blast radius in effect: InfluxDB is shared by fms-server, fms-consumer and grafana (their container state is watched by the blast-radius guard)
InfluxDB start-up time is unmeasured; recovery waits up to recovery_timeout_s (30 s) for fresh data
Data written while InfluxDB is down is lost unless the consumer buffers it (to be measured as a data gap)
Volumes (influxdb-data, influxdb-auth) persist across stop/start; the adapter never removes containers or volumes
